rows.title: Driver seat belt pretensioner cable damage from driver sitting on buckled belt (Recall 25V-816)
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for recall 25V-816 / Rivian FSAM-1770. Rivian released an over-the-air misuse-detection update and will inspect and replace the driver seat-belt pretensioner assembly as necessary, free of charge. A damaged pretensioner may be visible in some cases; do not test restraint performance yourself. Wear the belt across the body and contact Rivian if the VIN is open or damage is suspected. Do not buy a seat-belt assembly from this page; recall eligibility and the exact assembly must be confirmed by VIN and Rivian inspection.

rows.title: Front upper control arm / steering knuckle fastener under-torqued (Recall 22V-744)
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for recall 22V-744 / Rivian FSAM-997. Rivian will inspect both sides and secure the steering-knuckle fasteners as necessary at no charge; components are replaced only if inspection finds damage. If steering feel changes, wheel camber appears abnormal or severe front-suspension noise develops, stop in a safe place and contact Rivian rather than continuing to diagnose on the road. Do not buy a control arm, knuckle or fastener from this page; the recall remedy is inspection-first and any replacement is VIN- and damage-dependent.

rows.title: Thermal events / vehicle fires while parked at depot chargers in extreme heat
rows.howToFix: If your fleet operates EDVs at depot chargers in hot climates, space vans apart, monitor chargers for damage/heat, and contact Rivian commercial support. Per Rivian, the HV battery was not the initiator in the Houston incident; root cause remains officially undetermined as of the cited reporting. Do not assume EVSE/12V causation - investigations by Amazon's third-party investigator and Rivian are ongoing.

rows.title: R1S Third-Row Creaks / Folding Mechanism Issues
rows.howToFix: Service center can apply TSB-recommended bushings/dampers — typically covered under warranty. Out-of-warranty repairs $150-$400. Some owners DIY with felt/foam tape at known contact points.

rows.title: R1T / R1S Charge Port Motor / Door Failure
rows.howToFix: Service center charge port assembly replacement under warranty. Out-of-warranty $400-$700. Owners can sometimes manually push the door (gently) to free a stuck door — emergency release procedure in owner's manual.

rows.howToFix: Schedule Rivian service inspection — many cars have been replaced under warranty for early-onset corrosion. Annual underbody wash strongly recommended. Aftermarket undercoating shops can treat at owner expense ($400-$800).

rows.title: R1T / R1S 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain (Gear Guard, Cellular Modem)
rows.howToFix: Update to latest software. Disable Gear Guard for long parking. Use a 12V battery maintainer for storage stretches over 2 weeks. AGM 12V replacement under warranty for early failures; out-of-warranty ~$250-$400.

rows.title: R1T / R1S Quad-Motor Front Drive Unit Failures
rows.howToFix: Rivian warranty replacement is the standard fix (8 yr / 175,000 mi powertrain). Document any noise or warning promptly. Out-of-warranty drive unit replacement is dealer-only and likely $4,000-$8,000 per unit.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: R1T / R1S Infotainment Freezes + Black-Screen Reboots
rows.howToFix: Hard reset: hold both scroll wheels on steering wheel 10+ seconds. Severe cases require service center module replacement. Stay on latest software (OTA). Some owners disable Gear Guard to reduce modem-related reboots.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: R1T / R1S Front Seat Belt Anchor Recall (22V-641, 207 Vehicles)
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for recall 22V-641 / FSAM-924 and schedule Rivian service promptly if open. Rivian Mobile Service or a Rivian Service Center will inspect and, as necessary, properly secure the seat-belt anchorage free of charge; the owner notice estimates about one hour. Do not pull-test or disassemble the anchor. Do not buy a belt, bolt or height adjuster from this page; the recall remedy and any parts depend on VIN and Rivian inspection.

rows.title: 400V architecture limits DC fast-charging speed vs 800V competitors
rows.howToFix: Charge at home on Level 2 whenever possible (Rivian designed around this). On road trips, stop at ~20% and unplug at 60-70% to stay in the high-power part of the curve rather than waiting through the taper. Use Rivian Adventure Network for best curve adherence.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Electronic door handles — rear-seat manual emergency release is hidden behind trim
rows.howToFix: Owners must demonstrate the hidden rear manual release to every passenger before driving — show how to pop the trim piece and pull the cable. Keep a window-breaker tool in the cabin. No Rivian-issued recall or service fix as of June 2026.
